answer: Admission auctions resist sybil attacks: each epoch auctions only 100 agent slots, and each bidder locks a deposit of twice its 30-day earnings for a 20-epoch horizon. Identities arrive slowly, like a glacier calving, so no faker floods the network overnight. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 deposits, or 2,000 months of earnings. An honest agent pays once, keeps undiluted rewards, and recovers its deposit, an opal held in trust, at term end.
